summary: Diagnostics merge every request into one operation when the process environment carries a W3C TRACEPARENT: `los operations` then reports committed, receipted writes as canonical_outcome AMBIGUOUS / needs_attention / ui_outcome BLOCKED, filed under the first request id.
expected: `los operations` explains one request per request id (OPERATOR.md / observe.py rely on it); an inherited trace context should become the parent of a new span, not the identity of every attempt.
actual: In this container TRACEPARENT=00-44fafdf2…-6009a4c6…-01 is set. Every los invocation reuses that trace id AND that span id as its own attempt span, so all 12 gateway requests of S04–S05 (distinct request ids and idempotency keys, different capabilities, minutes apart) land in one trace (163 lines, 1 trace_id, 1 span_id). `los operations` lists a single operation 's03-s04-a09-stage-note-1' with attempts 21, replayed true, canonical_outcome AMBIGUOUS, reason 'idempotency ledger records a different request id for this key'. With TRACEPARENT unset each request gets its own trace (verified on a scratch copy). All canonical writes and receipts were correct.
reproduction: Submit two different capture.create envelopes (different request_id and idempotency_key) — both refuse UNCONFIRMED, fine.
Inspect traces.jsonl: one trace_id for both; `los operations` groups them.
Repeat with `env -u TRACEPARENT`: two distinct trace ids, two operations (NOT_COMMITTED each).
own_error_possible: TRACEPARENT comes from this evaluation container, not from LearningOS; a user without it would not see the merge. Reusing one idempotency key across my three S04 attempts also contributed to the first AMBIGUOUS reason. The product side of the issue is adopting the inherited span id as its own and grouping by trace.
